title: Scipio and Zama
objective: After this level you can explain how Scipio Africanus defeated Hannibal at Zama.
summary: Scipio took Spain, invaded Africa and beat Hannibal at Zama in 202 BCE. Carthage lost its empire and fleet and paid a huge indemnity.

cards.headline: Rome finally beat Hannibal by making him come home.
cards.body: For years, Rome couldn’t drive Hannibal out of Italy. So it went somewhere he wasn’t.

cards.headline: Take the war to Africa
cards.body: Publius Cornelius Scipio drove the Carthaginians out of Spain, Hannibal’s old base. Then he made a bold move: he invaded Africa and threatened Carthage itself. Carthage called Hannibal home to defend the city, and he was forced to leave Italy. Years of Roman armies couldn’t push him out. One threat to his own city did it.

cards.headline: Zama, 202 BCE
cards.body: At the Battle of Zama in 202 BCE, Scipio defeated Hannibal and won the Second Punic War, the war Hannibal had started back at Saguntum. Carthage paid heavily. It lost its overseas territories and most of its fleet, and it owed Rome a huge indemnity. The old queen of the sea was left with hardly a navy.
cards.callout: Zama, 202 BCE: the war is won

cards.fact: He was named for his victory.
cards.context: Scipio was given the name Africanus, after the continent where he won the war. Hannibal had carried the war into Italy. Scipio won it by carrying it to Africa, and the name stuck.

questions.explanation: Scipio beat Hannibal at Zama in 202 BCE and was named Africanus.

questions.prompt: How did Scipio get Hannibal out of Italy?

options.label: He defeated him in the Alps
He invaded Africa and threatened Carthage
He cut the Alpine passes
options.rationale: The key move was in Africa.

questions.explanation: By taking the war to Africa, Scipio forced Carthage to recall Hannibal to defend the city.

questions.prompt: From Level 23: Zama ended the war that began with which event?

options.label: The first secession of the plebs
The fight over Sicily in 264 BCE
options.rationale: That began the First Punic War.

options.label: Hannibal’s attack on Saguntum in Spain

questions.explanation: The Second Punic War was sparked by Hannibal’s attack on Saguntum, a Roman ally, and ended at Zama in 202 BCE.
